chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: 'I have acquired wealth in which I was uncertain (mixed) the permissible and the forbidden, and I intend to repent, but I do not know which part is permissible and which is forbidden, and they have become mixed up for me.' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Give the khums of your wealth, for indeed Allah, Exalted and Glorious, was pleased with the khums among things, and the rest of the wealth is for you.'
ai.seo_question: How to purify mixed halal and haram wealth when the specific portions cannot be distinguished?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (AS) provides a practical jurisprudential solution for mixed wealth where the specific haram portion is indistinguishable, ruling that paying the khums serves as a comprehensive purification (tazkiyah) for the entire sum. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease and certainty, allowing the owner to retain the remaining four-fifths as fully lawful, thereby resolving the uncertainty without requiring exhaustive tracing of every transaction. It underscores the spiritual and legal efficacy of khums not merely as a tax, but as a mechanism for cleansing mixed assets in commercial life.
